newsitem.title: USA: Leach says "very wary" of further Fed rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Leach says "very wary" of further Fed rate hikes.

text.p: House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach said on Monday that the U.S. economy is growing without signs of inflation, lessening the need for the Federal Reserve to raise short-term interest rates.

"The economy appears to be continuing to expand but without inflation raising any remarkable circumstances," the Iowa Republican said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "At this time, I'd be very wary of raising rates."
The central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee left interest rates unchanged at its last meeting May 20. The panel next meets July 1 and 2.
Leach said Congress' work to curb the federal deficit could eventually pave the way for the Fed to lower rates.

"As we move to lessen the deficit, you lay a basis for lower interest rates, not higher interest rates," Leach said in the interview. "To the degree Congress can keep on this track, there's a far better chance the Fed could actually reduce."
